title: QB2_B#q15 drew the IMSBC / IMDG line correctly in its own trap question and then contradicted it in On My Vessel by placing containerised cargo and flexitanks inside IMSBC scope
candidate_claim: Founder/GPT independent review of the Tranche 2 adjudication packet. QB2_B#q15's card correctly distinguishes IMSBC from IMDG in a Trap Question, but the On My Vessel block contradicts that and places containerised cargo and flexitanks inside IMSBC scope. The IMSBC Code governs solid bulk cargoes carried in bulk. A freight container or flexitank example must not be taught as an IMSBC operation merely because it is cargo. Correct ONLY the contradictory On My Vessel block and direct duplicate copies of that exact scope proposition; do not rewrite the main answer if it is already correct.
candidate_verdict: UPHELD, AND SETTLED BY A DEFINITION RATHER THAN BY A PROHIBITION - which is what makes the gate a fact rather than a judgement. SOLAS VI/1-1.2 defines a solid bulk cargo as one 'loaded directly into the cargo spaces of a ship without any intermediate form of containment', and the IMSBC Code's own application clause 1.4.1 anchors the Code to that definition. TWO INDEPENDENT LIMBS each exclude the published claim, and either alone is sufficient: a freight container IS an intermediate form of containment, so containerised cargo falls outside the definition however bulk-like the commodity looks; and a flexitank is LIQUID, so it also fails 'other than liquid or gas'. A flexitank is therefore excluded twice over - neither solid nor uncontained. The card's own Trap Question was already right and is preserved verbatim; the main answer was read in full and needed nothing.

authority.instrument: IMO resolution MSC.268(85), Adoption of the International Maritime Solid Bulk Cargoes (IMSBC) Code, adopted 4 December 2008, with the Code in its annex. Held at F:/RulesApp-Local-Input/true-source/03-imo-instruments/IMSBC-Code/_base-and-amendments/MSC.268(85).pdf, sha256 690a9dae8ffce1b00d695a4e839d60c3e1bd7c1d10bab3d33f96de85a116d9a5, 372 pages. The resolution reproduces the governing SOLAS regulations, which is where the operative definition below was read.
authority.operative_text_SOLAS_VI_1_1_2: p.9: '2 Solid bulk cargo means any cargo, other than liquid or gas, consisting of a combination of particles, granules or any larger pieces of material generally uniform in composition, which is loaded directly into the cargo spaces of a ship without any intermediate form of containment.'
authority.operative_text_IMSBC_1_4_1: p.7: '1.4.1 The provisions contained in this Code apply to all ships to which the SOLAS Convention, as amended, applies and that are carrying solid bulk cargoes as defined in regulation 1-1 of part A of chapter VI of the Convention.'
authority.operative_text_SOLAS_VI_1_2_1: p.9: 'Regulation 1-2 Requirements for the carriage of solid bulk cargoes other than grain. 1 The carriage of solid bulk cargoes other than grain shall be in compliance with the relevant provisions of the IMSBC Code.'
why_the_old_wording_is_wrong: A freight container is an intermediate form of containment. Cargo carried in boxes is therefore outside the SOLAS VI/1-1.2 definition and outside the Code, however bulk-like the commodity is. 'Containerized bulk shipments' is not an IMSBC category.

A flexitank is liquid cargo carried inside a freight container. It fails the definition on BOTH limbs - it is not solid, and it is not uncontained - so teaching it as an IMSBC operation is wrong twice over.

The error is not merely a mis-citation: it contradicts the card's own Trap Question two blocks earlier, which correctly says IMDG covers packaged form including containers while IMSBC governs loose un-packaged material loaded directly into bulk holds. A candidate reading the card in order is taught the rule and then shown it broken.
authority.what_actually_governs_the_ship: The replacement asserts only regimes that genuinely apply to a cellular containership and invents no Maersk procedure: the IMDG Code for dangerous goods in packaged form including in containers; the applicable container / CTU framework for packing and securing practice; and the approved Cargo Securing Manual. It closes by saying the answer comes from the Code and the ship types it governs rather than from bulk-carrier practice the writer does not have - which is true, and is the same truthful direction CORR-GPT-T1-GRAIN-20260904 took on q11's On My Vessel block.
authority.source_currentness: THE IMSBC CODE IS AN EVOLVING INSTRUMENT AND THIS RECORD DOES NOT PRETEND OTHERWISE. MSC.268(85) is the base Code; the corpus holds amendments through MSC.500(105). Amendment 08-25 (MSC.575(110)) is NOT held, and its status - voluntary application from 1 January 2026, envisaged entry into force 1 January 2027 - is already recorded in known_traps.md trap 55. IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT INTRODUCED HERE. The proposition written into the card is the base-Code scope definition at SOLAS VI/1-1.2, which no amendment in the held chain alters and which is not amendment-dependent. Nothing in this correction teaches a 2027 amendment as mandatory in September 2026, and nothing relies on amendment-specific text.
